title: spend-reservations.jsonl - one line of a run's reservation record
description: runs/<id>/spend-reservations.jsonl, appended by src/spend-reservations.js: one JSON object per line, each written whole with one write and fsynced. A 'reserved' line is the worst case of a paid call, written BEFORE the request is sent; a 'settled' line follows when the call returns or throws. A reserved line with no settled line is a call that was in flight when the process ended: it stays charged at its worst case in a resume's cap, council --spend and the spend report (once, at the larger of the two, when a usage file also carries its id). A settled line whose usage file was never written is counted too, at its settled figure, when its reserved line is in the folder. A settled line with no reserved line is damage to the file: it is counted nowhere, and `council --spend` names it. A last line with no newline is a torn write and is ignored. The file carries amounts, stage labels and provider/model only (and, on a reserved line written while per-provider spend caps are on, the provider id of the cap the call counts against), never task text or run content. Not tamper-evident: whoever can write the run folder can edit it. This schema describes one line.

id.description: r1, r2, ... per run folder; a resume continues after the ones already in the file.

usd.description: reserved: the call's worst case. settled: what it cost, or null when it is not known.

capName.description: reserved only, and only while per-provider spend caps are on (COUNCIL_SPEND_CAPS): the provider id of the cap this call counts against. Absent otherwise.

reachedProvider.description: settled only (0.8.4): the request reached the provider (an HTTP 5xx answered) though no usage figure came back; the usd is THC's count. Absent otherwise.

basis.description: settled only (0.8.4): what the settled usd stands for (src/counted-bases.js). Absent on a line written without one.

standsFor.description: reserved only (0.8.4): a worst-case line written to stand for a call whose record could not be written names the reservation it stands for, so one reader does not count that call twice. Absent otherwise.
